correctness.rationale: Just before vertex j arrives the i-subtree size W follows a two-color Pólya urn. Its first two rising factorial moments yield P(j descendant of i)=1/i and size-biased E[S_i(j)|A]=2j/(i+1); complement gives j/(i+1). A three-color Dirichlet–multinomial urn for vertices after j gives conditional cross-class covariance −n(n−j)ab/[j²(j+1)] and variance n(n−j)a(j−a)/[j²(j+1)]. As j is one initial singleton, averaging conditional Z yields covariances n(n−j)(i−1)/[(i+1)j(j+1)] on A and −n(n−j)/[(i+1)j(j+1)] off A. Their 1/i weighted cancellation is exact. Dependence is witnessed by S_i=n−i+1, where E[S_j]=(n−i+1)/(j−i+1)>n/j. i=1 or j=n gives deterministic subtree size. Independent complete parent-array enumeration n=4..7 verified each pair and signed formula exactly.

value.rationale: Nested versus disjoint descendant subtrees are natural dependent coordinates of a recursive growth tree. Exact zero covariance despite strict dependence, and conditioning that reveals opposite covariance signs, is a motivated structural warning against interpreting orthogonality as independence. Complete pairwise boundary classification is mathematically useful on its own.

final_claim: For any two fixed vertex-labelled descendant-subtree sizes in a uniform random recursive tree, unconditional covariance is zero, yet every nonboundary pair is dependent; conditioning on ancestry gives the stated exact strictly opposite positive/negative covariances.
